description_good_justification: README.md opens with a clear one-line description ('Cryptographic attestation of human cognitive involvement in digital content creation') and a 'What This Repository Contains' section describing the IETF drafts, CDDL schema, and docs. GitHub repo description via `gh api repos/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/proof-of-effort` matches: 'Cryptographic Proof of Effort (CPoE) — IETF Internet-Draft specification for verifiable attestation of human cognitive involvement in digital content creation, built on the RATS architecture (RFC 9334)'.
interact_justification: README.md links to GitHub Issues for feedback ('Feedback is welcome via GitHub Issues or the RATS mailing list') and to CONTRIBUTING.md for how to contribute. CONTRIBUTING.md gives fork/branch/PR/DCO steps.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'How to Contribute' section explains: report issues via GitHub issue tracker, fork + feature branch + PR against main, DCO sign-off required (git commit -s), and lists what to contribute (spec text, CDDL, docs, CI).
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Style Guidelines' section specifies kramdown-rfc and RFC 7322 conventions for draft text, RFC 8610 CDDL notation conventions, and requires DCO sign-off on every commit (enforced per CONTRIBUTING.md, though no DCO-check CI workflow file was found in .github/workflows/ to independently confirm enforcement).
floss_license_justification: LICENSE file contains the full Apache License 2.0 text. `gh api repos/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/proof-of-effort` reports license.spdx_id = 'Apache-2.0'.
floss_license_osi_justification: Apache License 2.0 is OSI-approved (https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0). Confirmed as the repo's declared license via LICENSE and LICENSE.md.
license_location_justification: LICENSE (full Apache-2.0 text) and LICENSE.md (pointer/summary noting IETF TLP also applies to draft-*.md files) both exist at the repository root, the standard location.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md (13K) documents purpose, protocol mechanics, and links to docs/architecture.md, cddl/cpoe.cddl, and integration docs under docs/integration/. README-W3C.md provides an additional W3C-audience overview.
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is the CBOR wire format for Evidence Packets and Attestation Results, formally documented in cddl/cpoe.cddl and cddl/swf.cddl (CDDL schema, machine-checked by .github/workflows/cddl.yml), plus prose specification in draft-condrey-cpoe-protocol.md and draft-condrey-cpoe-appraisal.md.
sites_https_justification: Repo URL (https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/proof-of-effort), GitHub Pages homepage (https://lf-decentralized-trust-labs.github.io/proof-of-effort/), and all documentation links observed in README.md use https:// URLs.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues (used actively, 21 open issues per `gh api repos/.../` open_issues_count) is URL-addressable, searchable, and open to any GitHub user without a proprietary client. `gh api repos/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/proof-of-effort --jq '.has_discussions'` also returns true, so GitHub Discussions is additionally enabled.
english_justification: All documentation (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, GOVERNANCE.md, drafts) and observed issue/PR titles (e.g. issues #121, #103, #94) are in English.
maintained_justification: `git log` shows commits through 2026-08-25 (most recent: 95977c2, 'ci: correct stale checkout version comments...'). `gh api repos/.../` pushed_at = 2026-08-25T09:25:18Z. Regular dependabot merges and external contributor PRs (christianrp45, tyche-dev, Deepak8858, HuiNeng6) throughout June-Aug 2026 show ongoing activity within the last 12 months.
repo_public_justification: Repository is public at https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/proof-of-effort, readable without authentication; confirmed via `gh api` and `git remote -v` (origin = git@github.com:LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/proof-of-effort.git).
repo_track_justification: Git (per .git/) records author, committer, timestamp, and full diff for every change. `git log` output shows author emails, dates, and PR merge references for each commit.
repo_interim_justification: `git log --oneline -20` shows a continuous stream of incremental commits (docs fixes, CI fixes, dependency bumps, review-comment follow-ups) between the tagged points, not just squashed release commits.
repo_distributed_justification: Repository uses Git, a distributed version control system, hosted on GitHub.
version_unique_justification: No GitHub Releases exist (`gh api repos/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/proof-of-effort/releases` returns `[]`). The two existing tags (cpop-jitter-v0.2.1, cpop-protocol-v0.1.1) are explicitly flagged as stray/inconsistent by open issue #114 ('Reconcile the stray cpop-* release tags with what this repository currently is'), and impl/posme/Cargo.toml is still at version 0.1.0 with no corresponding tag. IETF drafts do carry unique version identifiers (e.g. draft-condrey-cpoe-protocol-NN) via the datatracker submission path in .github/workflows/publish.yml, but the project as a whole has not yet established a consistent, reconciled versioning scheme for its own releases.
version_semver_justification: impl/posme/Cargo.toml uses SemVer-shaped version = "0.1.0", but no crate has been published/released under a scheme, and the stray git tags (cpop-jitter-v0.2.1, cpop-protocol-v0.1.1) do not correspond to any current crate/draft naming (issue #114). No consistent SemVer or CalVer policy is documented anywhere (CONTRIBUTING.md, GOVERNANCE.md).
version_tags_justification: Only stray tags cpop-jitter-v0.2.1 and cpop-protocol-v0.1.1 existed; they were removed (see #114) and this repository tags no releases.
release_notes_justification: N/A: no discrete numbered releases exist yet (`gh api repos/.../releases` returns `[]`); the project is at the pre-adoption Internet-Draft stage per README.md ('Status: These are individual Internet-Drafts, not yet adopted by any IETF working group'). CHANGELOG.md exists in Keep-a-Changelog format but only has an 'Unreleased' section and one dated entry describing initial repo creation, not a tagged release.
release_notes_vulns_justification: N/A: no discrete releases exist yet, so release_notes itself is N/A, and there are no publicly known vulnerabilities to date (no GitHub Security Advisories found via `gh api repos/.../security-advisories`, which returned an empty list).
report_process_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Reporting Issues' directs users to the GitHub issue tracker (https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/proof-of-effort/issues). .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ contains bug_report.yml and feature_request.yml structured templates.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is used for individual issue tracking; `gh api repos/.../` shows has_issues true with 21 open issues, and `gh api .../issues` lists numbered, individually tracked issues (e.g. #121, #118, #117, #94) distinct from PRs.
report_responses_justification: Reviewing `gh api .../issues?state=all` for non-maintainer-authored issues in the last several months: #121 (christianrp45, 1 comment), #103 (christianrp45, 3 comments), #97 (christianrp45, 1 comment), #94 (christianrp45, 5 comments), #93 (tyche-dev, 1 comment), #92 (tyche-dev, 1 comment) all show maintainer engagement (comments present, several merged as PRs). No open external-contributor issue in the sample was left with zero response.
enhancement_responses_justification: External feature-request style issues/PRs from contributors (#121 'propose Composite Device profile', #103 'LICET wearable Attester topology', #94 'T2 corroboration', #93/#92 forgery-cost and calibration proposals) all show comment activity and, in several cases (#97, #103 related PRs), were merged into main, indicating enhancement requests are being reviewed and responded to.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues provides a public, URL-addressable, searchable archive of all reports and their discussion threads at https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/proof-of-effort/issues (open and closed), confirmed via `gh api .../issues?state=all`.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md is a detailed, published vulnerability disclosure policy at the repo root: security team contact, report intake channels, embargo process, CVE/CNA process, and GitHub Security Advisory workflow, aligned with the LF Decentralized Trust Security Policy.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md 'Report Intakes' section documents two private channels: emailing security@lists.lfdecentralizedtrust.org, and opening a private GitHub Security Advisory ('Security' tab), with a link to GitHub's private-vulnerability-reporting docs.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: N/A: no vulnerability reports have been received. `gh api repos/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/proof-of-effort/security-advisories` returns an empty list, so there is no track record yet to evaluate against the 14-day response commitment (SECURITY.md commits to 2 business days acknowledgment).
build_justification: The Rust crates (impl/posme, impl/posme-ref) build with a standard `cargo build`; verified directly: `cd impl/posme/impl/posme && cargo build` completed with 'Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 5.47s' and no errors. The IETF drafts also have a working automated build via Makefile + lib/main.mk (martinthomson/i-d-template) invoked by .github/workflows/ghpages.yml and publish.yml.
build_common_tools_justification: Rust crates use standard `cargo`/`rustc` per impl/posme/Cargo.toml. Draft build uses the community-standard i-d-template/kramdown-rfc/xml2rfc toolchain documented in CONTRIBUTING.md ('Build locally with `make`... requires xml2rfc, kramdown-rfc, and the i-d-template toolchain').
build_floss_tools_justification: cargo/rustc, kramdown-rfc, xml2rfc, and i-d-template (referenced in CONTRIBUTING.md and Makefile) are all FLOSS tools; no proprietary compiler or build tool is required.
test_justification: impl/posme/src/lib.rs contains 8 unit tests (verified passing: `cd impl/posme && cargo test` -> 'PASS: 9 passed'), which satisfies the 'at least one automated FLOSS test suite' half of this criterion. However the second half — documented how to run it — fails: `grep -rn "cargo test" README.md CONTRIBUTING.md docs/ impl/` finds zero references anywhere in the repo's documentation to running the test suite, so this MUST criterion is Unmet as a conjunction.
test_invocation_justification: impl/posme/src/lib.rs contains 8 unit tests (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at line 283, individual `#[test]` functions at lines 287, 306, 326, 345, 366, 384, 403, 420), verified passing via `cd impl/posme/impl/posme && cargo test` (result: 'PASS: 9 passed'). This is invocable the standard way for Rust (`cargo test`), but `grep -rn "cargo test" README.md CONTRIBUTING.md docs/ impl/` found zero matches: the invocation is not documented anywhere in the repo, so a new contributor has no written instruction to discover it.
test_most_justification: The 9 passing tests in impl/posme/src/lib.rs cover core hash/merkle/prove/verify functions, but impl/posme-ref/src/main.rs (a separate reference-implementation crate) has zero #[test] functions (`grep -rn '#\[test\]' impl/posme-ref/src` returned nothing), and the protocol/appraisal specification itself has no conformance test suite beyond docs/conformance/ (not inspected as executable tests). Coverage of the overall project's functionality is partial.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: No CI workflow in .github/workflows/ runs `cargo test`, `cargo build`, or any Rust check (`grep -rl "cargo" .github/workflows/` matches only cddl.yml, which runs `cargo install cddl` for CDDL schema validation, not the project's own crates). CHANGELOG.md's 2026-03-17 entry claims 'Rust CI workflow for build, test, clippy, and format checks' was added, but no such workflow file exists in .github/workflows/ today — this is a documentation/reality mismatch, not evidence of CI.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Submitting Changes' and 'Style Guidelines' sections describe how to submit spec/CDDL/CI changes but do not state any policy that new major functionality (e.g. new Rust code) must come with tests.
tests_are_added_justification: No documented test-addition policy exists (see test_policy), and there is no CI gate enforcing it (see test_continuous_integration), so there is no mechanism to verify recent major changes were required to add tests. The most recent substantive Rust PRs (#76 'use workspace.package inheritance', #75 'Add Clone and PartialEq to Error enums', #74 'Add Hash derive and Display impl') are refactors/derives rather than new functionality that would exercise a test-added policy either way.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md contains no mention of a testing policy or requirement to add tests for new functionality (confirmed by reading the full file; only build/style/DCO instructions are present).
warnings_justification: No clippy configuration exists (`find . -iname clippy.toml -o -iname .clippy.toml` found nothing under impl/), no `#![deny(warnings)]` or `#![warn(...)]` attributes in impl/posme/src/lib.rs or impl/posme-ref/src/main.rs (grep for 'deny\|warn\|clippy' returned no matches), and no CI workflow runs `cargo clippy` (see test_continuous_integration). Rust's default `rustc` warnings are on, but no stricter FLOSS linter (clippy, which exists and is standard for Rust) is enabled.
warnings_fixed_justification: `cd impl/posme/impl/posme && cargo build` produced 'Finished ... target(s) in 5.47s' with zero warnings in the output, so the default rustc warnings that are enabled are clean. (Note: this is a weaker signal than clippy, which is not run — see `warnings`.)
warnings_strict_justification: No evidence of maximally strict warning settings: no `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, no `#![deny(warnings)]`, no clippy.toml, and no CI enforcement (see `warnings` and `test_continuous_integration`).
know_secure_design_justification: The primary maintainer (David Condrey, per MAINTAINERS.md and git commit history) authored substantial security-design content: draft-condrey-cpoe-appraisal.md includes a 'Forgery Cost Bounds (Quantified Security)' section (line 949) with sub-sections on sequential work function cost, behavioral evidence synthesis cost, and hardware attestation cost — an explicit adversarial/economic security model. Both draft-condrey-cpoe-protocol.md (line 2012) and draft-condrey-cpoe-appraisal.md (line 1922) have mandatory IETF 'Security Considerations' sections. anc/posme-attack-brief.md is a dedicated 'PoSME Independent Security Assessment Brief' analyzing the primitive's threat model for outside review.
know_common_errors_justification: draft-condrey-cpoe-protocol.md's Security Considerations (line 2012) and draft-condrey-cpoe-appraisal.md's (line 1922) discuss specific attack classes (e.g. 'Late Initialization' content-substitution attack at appraisal.md line 854, addressed via 'Retype defenses, witness-anchored nonce binding, beacon binding'). anc/posme-attack-brief.md and anc/posme-attack.py document adversarial analysis of the PoSME primitive. Code shows deliberate mitigation practices: domain-separated hashing to prevent cross-protocol collisions (impl/posme/src/hash.rs: 'Domain-separated BLAKE3 hash... prevents cross-protocol hash collisions').
crypto_published_justification: cddl/cpoe.cddl specifies only publicly published, standard algorithms: Ed25519 signing keys (line 41), SHA-256 (lines 107, 415), HMAC (line 118), COSE_Sign1 per RFC 9052 (lines 10, 185, 233, 269, 308), and Argon2id (line 432, 'swf-argon2id-sha256: 1, ; MTI for all tiers'). impl/posme/src/hash.rs uses BLAKE3, a public, widely reviewed hash function.
crypto_call_justification: impl/posme/Cargo.toml depends on the published `blake3` crate (dependencies: blake3 = "1") rather than reimplementing hashing; the spec calls out standard COSE/Ed25519/Argon2id primitives (cddl/cpoe.cddl) rather than defining bespoke crypto.
crypto_floss_justification: All referenced algorithms (Ed25519, SHA-256, HMAC, Argon2id, BLAKE3, COSE per RFC 9052) have mature FLOSS implementations (e.g. Rust `ed25519-dalek`, `sha2`, `argon2`, `blake3` crates, all used in impl/posme via the FLOSS `blake3` crate already in Cargo.toml).
crypto_keylength_justification: cddl/cpoe.cddl specifies signing-public-key as 32 bytes (line 41, Ed25519 — 256-bit, exceeds NIST minimums through 2030) and hash outputs as 32-byte SHA-256/BLAKE3 digests; no smaller/legacy key sizes are used as defaults.
crypto_working_justification: `grep -rniE 'md5|sha-?1[^0-9]|rc4|single-des|dual_ec' cddl/ draft-condrey-cpoe-*.md` returned no matches: no broken algorithm (MD4/MD5/SHA-1/single-DES/RC4/Dual_EC_DRBG) is used by default. Default mechanisms are SHA-256/BLAKE3/Ed25519/Argon2id/COSE per cddl/cpoe.cddl.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Same grep as crypto_working confirms no SHA-1 usage; defaults use SHA-256 and BLAKE3. No CBC-in-SSH or comparable flagged pattern appears in the spec, which is not an SSH-related protocol.
crypto_pfs_justification: N/A: CPoE is an attestation/evidence-signing protocol (COSE_Sign1 signatures over evidence packets, per cddl/cpoe.cddl), not a session/transport key-agreement protocol, so perfect forward secrecy for key agreement does not apply to its cryptographic design.
crypto_password_storage_justification: N/A: the project does not store user passwords; it is an evidence/attestation format and reference implementation, not an authentication system.
crypto_random_justification: The specification requires randomness at multiple points (draft-condrey-cpoe-protocol.md: 'random salt of at least 16 bytes' at line 1322, 'locally-generated 32-byte random nonce' at line 1684, 'challenge-nonce (128+ bits)' at cddl line 1187), but the text does not explicitly mandate a CSPRNG, and the reference Rust implementation (impl/posme/src, impl/posme-ref/src) contains no `rand`, `OsRng`, `thread_rng`, or nonce-generation code at all (`grep -rn 'rand|random|OsRng|thread_rng|nonce' impl/posme/src impl/posme-ref/src` matched only a doc comment, not actual RNG usage) — the reference implementation does not yet implement nonce/salt generation, so CSPRNG use cannot be verified in code.
delivery_mitm_justification: The repository is retrieved via `git clone` over https (https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/proof-of-effort) or ssh (git@github.com:...), both of which counter MITM. `cargo` dependency downloads (verified during `cargo build`) use https via crates.io.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No unsigned, hash-only integrity check delivered over plain http was found; all delivery channels observed (git+https/ssh, crates.io via cargo/https) use TLS/SSH transport, not plain HTTP with only a hash.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No publicly known unpatched medium-or-higher vulnerabilities exist: `gh api repos/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/proof-of-effort/security-advisories` returns an empty list, and dependency-bump PRs from dependabot (visible throughout `git log`, e.g. #109, #110, #120, #122) are merged promptly (typically within days), keeping GitHub Actions dependencies current.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerabilities have been reported against this project to date (`gh api repos/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/proof-of-effort/security-advisories` returns an empty list), so none are outstanding; vacuously met with no counter-evidence. This key has no 'N/A ok' allowance in the criteria spec, so it is recorded as Met rather than N/A.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: `git ls-files | grep -Ei '\.venv/|\.env$|id_rsa|\.pem$|\.p12$|credentials'` returned no matches — no credential-shaped files are tracked in git. .gitignore excludes .venv/ and other local artifacts. No hardcoded secrets were observed in any file read during this review (README.md, SECURITY.md, workflows, Rust source).
static_analysis_justification: Rust has a mature FLOSS static analysis tool (clippy, bundled with rustup) but it is not run anywhere: no clippy.toml exists, no CI workflow invokes `cargo clippy` (`grep -rl cargo .github/workflows/` matches only cddl.yml, for `cargo install cddl` schema validation — not a lint/analysis step). .github/workflows/scorecard.yml runs OpenSSF Scorecard, which assesses supply-chain/repo posture, not source-code static analysis, and its SARIF upload step (`github/codeql-action/upload-sarif`) only uploads Scorecard's own results — no actual CodeQL code-scanning job exists in .github/workflows/.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: N/A: since no static analysis tool is currently applied (see `static_analysis`), whether it includes common-vulnerability rules cannot be evaluated.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: N/A: no static analysis tool is applied (see `static_analysis`), so there are no findings to have fixed in a timely way.
static_analysis_often_justification: No static analysis tool runs on any commit or on a schedule for the project's own source (cddl.yml only validates CDDL schema syntax on push/PR to cddl/**; scorecard.yml runs OpenSSF Scorecard weekly and on push to main, but that is a supply-chain/metadata scanner, not source static analysis).
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis tool (e.g. sanitizers, fuzzing) is applied before releases; no CI workflow or documented process runs any dynamic-analysis tool against impl/posme or impl/posme-ref.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: N/A: the delivered Rust implementation contains no `unsafe` code (`grep -rn unsafe impl/posme/src impl/posme-ref/src` returned no matches), so memory-unsafe-code dynamic analysis (e.g. ASan/Valgrind) does not apply to it. Note: anc/posme-cuda-bench.cu is CUDA C++, but it lives under anc/ (ancillary benchmark/research material, not the delivered protocol implementation) and was excluded from this assessment on that basis.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic analysis is run at all (see `dynamic_analysis`), so no assertion-enabling configuration for such a tool exists.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: N/A: no dynamic analysis tool is applied (see `dynamic_analysis`), so there are no findings to have fixed.
